note: Machine-readable capability ledger for the Cognitia GTM Control Plane. This file is the source of truth and is mechanically validated by apps/api/src/truthReport.test.ts: status values must be in the enum, every evidence pointer must resolve to a real file in the repo, blocked_external entries must name a blocker and an unblock step, unverified entries must give a reason, and the summary counts must equal the capabilities. If code or evidence is renamed/removed, the test fails until this report is corrected.

legend.implemented: Built in-repo and guarded by a test that fails in CI if the behavior regresses.
legend.partial: Some of the capability is real and tested; a named portion is not yet built in-repo.
legend.blocked_external: Cannot be truthfully completed in-repo: requires external credentials, account/admin configuration, repo settings, or an out-of-repo lane.
legend.unverified: Not yet attempted or proven in this environment; feasibility is uncertain and is stated honestly rather than claimed.

capabilities.title: Governed write lifecycle (preflight → preview → approval → execute → undo)
capabilities.summary: Every CRM write flows through a zero-write preflight, a byte-equal preview, a mandatory closed-enum approval reason, idempotent provenance-stamped execution, and reversible undo. Denials are audited.

capabilities.title: Enforced integration kill switch (ENF-1)
capabilities.summary: An integration connection can be paused; while paused, writes are refused at the enforcement point, not just hidden in the UI. Connection status is tenant-scoped.

capabilities.title: Preflight simulation is provably zero-write (SIM-1)
capabilities.summary: Preflight proposes a plan without persisting any action rows; the ledger is unchanged after a preflight run.

capabilities.title: V1 scope fence: CRM write-back only, no email (FEN-1..3)
capabilities.summary: The email path is fenced out of the V1 composition in code, not just docs: no email webhook route, and the V1 adapter registry has no executable email handler. A control case proves the gate works.

capabilities.title: Repository contract parity (in-memory and real Postgres via PGlite)
capabilities.summary: The same contract assertions run against the in-memory repository and the Kysely repository over real Postgres (PGlite/WASM), so behavior cannot drift between the test reference and production.

capabilities.title: Golden evaluation gate
capabilities.summary: A golden dataset run gates governance behavior; the trust packet re-runs it live as embedded evidence.

capabilities.title: Run/plan rollups (RUN-1)
capabilities.summary: A Mira run groups its proposed actions into one reviewable unit with a governance rollup; fully_reviewed flips only when nothing is awaiting a decision.

capabilities.title: Run detail / action timeline (RUN-2)
capabilities.summary: GET /agent-runs/:id returns the run plus its proposed actions in created order and the governance rollup. Read-only, viewer-allowed, tenant-scoped.

capabilities.title: Integration sync history + opportunities visibility (EVID-1)
capabilities.summary: Read-only, tenant-scoped surfaces for integration sync runs (newest first) and opportunities; account context carries its opportunities. No new write paths.

capabilities.title: Audit trail visibility
capabilities.summary: GET /audit returns tenant-scoped audit events, including audited denials from the governance flow.

capabilities.title: Tamper-evident audit chain (SEC-1)
capabilities.summary: Every audit event is hash-linked to its predecessor per tenant; the repository computes the chain on insert (callers cannot forge or skip a link) and a unique (tenant_id, prev_hash) index forbids forks. GET /audit/verify (viewer-allowed) recomputes the chain from genesis; mutation, deletion, forking, or stripped chain fields are detected — proven against real Postgres via raw-SQL tampering. Tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof: external anchoring of the chain tip is future work.

capabilities.title: Decision finality + verified-user audit attribution (SEC-1)
capabilities.summary: The ledger enforces a decision state machine: only proposed actions can be approved/rejected (no rejected→approved flips, no duplicate decision labels), and a rolled-back action can never be re-executed on its stale approval — refusals are audited. Audit actor refs carry the verified user identity from the session principal (user:<userRef>), not just the role; session claims are strictly validated (closed role enum, typed tenant/user ids) so malformed tokens fail closed. Unimplemented seam endpoints return 501 instead of fake success.

capabilities.title: Exportable trust packet (TRUST-2)
capabilities.summary: A live-derived JSON artifact with control attestations (each citing a test file enforced to exist), an embedded real eval run, scorecards, governance matrix, and kill-switch state; contains no raw PII.

capabilities.title: Per-segment governance scorecards (LEARN-1)
capabilities.summary: Per-segment (action type × risk) metrics with a read-only autonomy indicator that grants nothing and is wired to no execution path.

capabilities.title: Trust metrics strip (MET-1)
capabilities.summary: Live-derived approval/execution/rollback metrics for the console header strip.

capabilities.title: Decision rationale (WHY-1)
capabilities.summary: Each proposed action exposes a structured rationale (evidence + guardrail results) so an operator sees why it was proposed.

capabilities.title: Grounded CRM note action (CRM-NOTE-1)
capabilities.summary: A second governed action type (grounded note) proposed alongside the task action, under the same approval and fence guarantees.

capabilities.title: Integration readiness surface (RDY-1)
capabilities.summary: A read-only readiness view reports whether an integration is configured and connectable, without exposing secrets.

capabilities.title: Auth, roles, and tenant scoping
capabilities.summary: Read routes require a tenant (401 otherwise) and are tenant-scoped; mutating routes require operator/owner (403 otherwise). Cross-tenant reads return empty.

capabilities.title: Deploy smoke gate
capabilities.summary: A smoke matrix asserts the expected status for key routes/roles, so a misconfigured deployment (e.g. an exposed mutating route) fails the gate.

capabilities.title: HubSpot webhook ingest
capabilities.summary: Inbound HubSpot webhooks are verified and ingested idempotently into the event log and external object map.

capabilities.title: HubSpot read/sync + write-plan (exercised against fakes)
capabilities.summary: The HubSpot adapter's sync, write-plan, and HTTP client logic are exercised end-to-end against fake transports. This proves the code path; it does NOT prove a live account (see live-hubspot-credentials).

capabilities.title: Regression scenario candidate from rejections (REGR-1)
capabilities.summary: A rejected action can be exported as an anonymized regression-scenario candidate to grow the eval set.

capabilities.title: Batch approve/reject with a shared reason (UX-2)
capabilities.summary: Multiple actions can be approved or rejected in one call with a shared closed-enum reason; partial failures are surfaced per id.

capabilities.title: README evidence honesty guard (RDM-1)
capabilities.summary: Every test file cited as evidence in the root README must exist; a renamed or deleted test fails CI until the README is corrected.

capabilities.title: Live HubSpot connection (real account, real OAuth tokens, real sync)
capabilities.summary: The adapter and token-provider code paths are implemented and tested against fakes, but proving a real sync requires live HubSpot credentials and account configuration that cannot exist in-repo.
capabilities.blocker: Requires a HubSpot account/app, OAuth client credentials, and operator authorization — external secrets and account admin access that must not be faked.
capabilities.unblock: Provision a HubSpot app, supply client id/secret + scopes as environment secrets, connect a tenant, then run the live sync and capture the sync_run as evidence.

capabilities.title: Production deploy + branch protection on the live repo
capabilities.summary: CI (format + typecheck + full vitest) runs on every push/PR, but a production deployment target and enforced branch protection depend on GitHub repo settings and a deploy identity outside this repo.
capabilities.blocker: Requires GitHub repository admin settings (required checks, branch protection) and a hosting/deploy identity with secrets.
capabilities.unblock: Configure required status checks + branch protection in repo settings, add the deploy target and its secrets, then record a successful deployment.

capabilities.title: Reconciled design-system implementation (tokens/stylesheet layer)
capabilities.summary: The console uses inline styles; the reconciled warm Swiss-minimal design system is not present as a token/stylesheet layer in this repo. It is owned by a separate (Codex) design lane.
capabilities.blocker: Out-of-repo lane: the design-system source/tokens are produced elsewhere and not yet landed here.
capabilities.unblock: Land the design tokens/stylesheet layer from the design lane, then migrate the console off inline styles behind it.

capabilities.title: Accessibility checks for the primary operator route (jsdom + axe-core)
capabilities.summary: The approvals route is rendered in jsdom and scanned by axe-core in two states: the unauthenticated sign-in shell (no token, no network) and the authenticated approval queue (token seeded, on-mount fetches stubbed so the real action table with per-row select controls renders). Both assert no serious/critical violations and accessible control names. Browser-free: catches markup/ARIA/label/landmark regressions in CI without a browser binary. Layout-dependent rules remain real-browser work.

capabilities.title: Real-browser end-to-end smoke (Playwright over a running app)
capabilities.summary: No real-browser (Playwright/Chromium) end-to-end smoke exists. The jsdom+axe layer (a11y-checks-primary-route) covers accessibility of static markup, but layout-dependent behavior and full-page navigation across authenticated state are not exercised in a real browser.
capabilities.reason: A real browser engine requires downloading a Chromium binary and standing up the Next.js app; this has not been attempted or proven in this environment and is stated honestly rather than assumed. The npm registry is reachable (axe-core/testing-library installed), so this is likely feasible, but the browser-binary download and app-server harness remain to be verified.
